Subject: Private offer: tiered metering + reseller commission concession

Rachel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. StratoTech is interested in moving forward with a private offer for our analytics product team. A couple of asks from procurement and our reseller:

- We need a clear SKU packaging for a tiered metering model (base seat + compute tokens). Can you confirm how Redwood maps SKU billing to marketplace SKUs?
- Our reseller (CloudChannel) expects a 15% pass-through on list price. Your standard is 12% per docs — is there room to accommodate 15% for the first 12 months if we commit to a 24-month total term and $425k ARR?
- Procurement will need a PDF of the private offer and a keyed DocuSign PO link once terms are agreed.

Can you loop in finance for SKU/metering examples and an initial pricing workbook?

Asha
Asha Patel
Head of Cloud Procurement, StratoTech
asha.patel@stratotech.com
+1 415-555-0198

Subject: Re: Private offer: tiered metering + reseller commission concession

Hi Asha —

Great to reconnect. Appreciate the clarity on the ask. High-level answers while I pull the workbook:

- SKU mapping: Redwood exposes two marketplace SKUs per billing model: a BASE_SEAT SKU (flat per-seat monthly) and a TOKEN_METER SKU (per-1k tokens). For private offers we can bundle them into a single composite SKU that the marketplace recognizes; in practice we provide a mapping table that shows how on-invoice consumption maps to our internal metering. I will attach an example mapping and a draft bundle definition.

- Channel margin: our standard reseller pass-through is 12% on list price. For a committed 24-month deal at $425k ARR with a 12-month front-loaded commit, we can make a one-time concession to 15% for months 1–12 if StratoTech signs the 24-month term and agrees to an annual true-up clause. We would need this explicitly written into the private offer as a commission override line item.

- Docs/PO: I can produce the PDF private offer and kick off a DocuSign envelope once we lock the final SKU bundle and margin language.

Ben — tagging you for the workbook and a suggested bundle definition. Naomi, can you confirm accounting treatment (escrow credits / true-up cadence) and whether we need a special invoice flow?

Next steps: Ben to upload a pricing_workbook; Naomi to confirm invoicing cadence; I will draft the private offer PDF and share. If that timeline works I can have a draft by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.inference

Rachel / Asha —

Uploading the workbook and a couple of scenario tabs: base seat + per-token metering, and an alternate flat-seat-plus-burst model (useful if you expect spiky ingest). Key notes in the workbook:

- Tab 'TieredMetering': shows list price, proposed private-offer list price (we usually apply a 10% uplift to marketplace list to preserve margin in pass-through), and the reseller commission row. I added a 'commission_override' cell where we can set 15% for months 1–12 and 12% thereafter.
- Tab 'EscrowCredits': outlines a simple crediting approach for overage refunds tied to true-ups (quarterly).
- Tab 'DocFlow': suggested invoice -> reseller pass-through -> StratoTech accounting path; requires our billing system to emit a reseller ID on invoice lines (we can do this).

I attached: pricing_workbook_stratotech.xlsx and RI_PrivateOffer_StratoTech_20260817.pdf (draft with bundle defs).

Open question for StratoTech: do you want the commission applied to list price or net-of-discount? We typically do list price but will accept net-of-discount if legal needs to avoid double-counting credits.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Deals Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.inference

Attachments: pricing_workbook_stratotech.xlsx (workbook, 42KB), RI_PrivateOffer_StratoTech_20260817.pdf (draft private offer, 95KB)

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer: tiered metering + reseller commission concession

Thanks Ben — received the workbook and draft private offer. Quick responses after a procurement sync this morning:

- Commission basis: we prefer commission on list price to keep the reseller economics simple. 15% for months 1–12 in exchange for the 24-month commitment and $425k ARR is acceptable to StratoTech.
- Escrow/true-up: quarterly true-ups are fine; procurement would like a 30-day invoice SLA for credits.
- DocuSign: please send the final private offer PDF with the commission_override line and I'll circulate to our CFO for signature. CloudChannel is ready to accept 15% for the first year.

If you can update the PDF to include the explicit commission_override row and the quarterly true-up + 30-day credit SLA, I can route for signature today. Also please confirm the marketplace SKU IDs so our procurement system can register the SKU.

Asha
Asha Patel
Head of Cloud Procurement, StratoTech
